## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

We need to build a 3D Dragon Ball-like anime game for phones/tablets. Pure static HTML is simplest — use Three.js via CDN? Need offline-safe. We have network? Let's check whether node_modules could be installed via npm (vite). But default start supports static html. Using CDN may fail in capture if no network. Better to vendor three.js locally. Check if npm can install three. Let's test network.

Design plan: A 3D arena brawler / flight combat game "Dragon Orb Z" with cel-shaded anime look:
- Third-person flight/arena combat on floating island? Phone/tablet touch controls.
- Mechanics: player hovers in arena, enemies (saibamen-like) spawn, tap buttons: punch/kick combo, energy blast (ki), dash, charge/transform (power up with aura), lock-on. Health bars, power bar, score, waves.
- Visual: cel shading via toon materials, outline via backside mesh, sky gradient, floating islands, rocks, energy orb collectibles, particle trails, bloom? Keep performant. Use Three.js with EffectComposer? Maybe skip postprocessing for mobile perf, but use additive sprites for glow.

Camera: behind/above third person; joystick left to move, right side buttons. Drag right side to rotate camera. Lock-on auto target.

Gameplay loop: waves of enemies spawn on floating arena, player fights; collect 7 dragon orbs dropped? Could have "Dragon Orb" pickups that fill meter; collect 7 then Shenron appears? For scope: Wave-based "Tournament" with 7 dragon balls collected from defeated enemies, when all 7 -> wish: full heal + power boost, then boss wave.

Make it genuinely playable: input, collision, damage, combo, dodge/dash with i-frames, ki blast projectiles, enemy AI (approach, attack, ranged ki), boss with slam and beam.

Layer UI: title screen with animated character (hero render?), start button. HUD: health, ki, wave, dragon ball icons, combo. Pause. Game over/victory.

Need to verify in Chromium with WebGL (SwiftShader likely). Use screenshots at 390x844 mobile and maybe desktop 1280. Note phone/tablet — responsive touch controls, also keyboard for desktop testing.

Technical: three.js local. Let's check npm install three. We can just download three.module.js from unpkg using fetch. Prefer npm install, then copy build files into vendor. But if we use package.json without vite, default start errors "Unsupported package project". So no package.json at root, or we use static with an import map to vendor/three.module.js. Copy three files into vendor/.

Let's test network access.

Also think about assets: no external models. Build characters from primitives with toon shading: hero Goku-like: orange gi, blue undershirt, spiky black hair, tail? Careful: "dragon ball like anime game" — make an original anime-inspired spiky-haired martial artist, not literal licensed characters. Name "Dragon Orb: Celestial Clash", hero "Kai". Enemies: alien "Saibra" green creatures? Keep original: "Void Oni" purple creatures. Boss: "Onyx Warlord".

Character construction: group with body, gi top (orange), belt (blue), pants, boots, head (skin), spiky hair (cones), arms; animate limbs procedurally (walk/hover bob, punch, kick, blast pose). Cel shading via MeshToonMaterial with gradientMap 3-tone DataTexture; outlines via clone mesh with BackSide black material scaled 1.03 (this doubles draw calls; characters maybe 10 -> fine).

Arena: floating rocky island with grass top? Dragon Ball inspired: rocky plateau with pillars, sky with gradient shader dome, floating rocks in distance, clouds. Sun/ambient. Ground disc with radial texture (canvas). Add ring-out? Boundaries with invisible walls / pushback. Arena radius ~18.

Combat design details:
- Player position on ground plane y=0, move with joystick relative to camera yaw. Speed 6. Facing toward target when locked.
- Camera: orbit camera controlled by right-side drag; default follow behind player with yaw controlled, pitch ~18°, distance 9, look at player +1.5. On mobile drag right half rotates camera. Joystick left.
- Buttons: PUNCH (3-hit combo), KI (hold to charge? tap ki blast), DASH, POWER (transform/charge super). Simpler: Attack button, Blast button, Dash button, Charge/Power button.
- Ki bar regenerates; blast costs 15, power-up costs full? Transform at full ki -> Super form for 12s: glowing gold hair, aura, damage up, speed up.
- Combo counter for successive hits.
- Auto lock-on nearest enemy; attack aims at target within range. Punch does short-range melee hit with visual shockwave; blasts homing slightly.
- Enemies: types: Grunt (melee, 40hp) and Sniper (ranged, 30hp). Boss 300hp with patterns.
- Waves: 1: 3 grunts; 2: 4 mixed; 3: 5; boss. Each defeated enemy drops a dragon ball (star ball) that flies to player when close; count 7. Maybe drop orbs every enemy until 7; when 7 collected: wish -> heal + shockwave clearing, "Shenron" dragon silhouette in sky? Could create a giant serpentine dragon made of segments that flies across sky for 5s, granting heal, then reset orb count. Nice wow moment.

- Health 100, enemy attacks reduce 8-12. Death -> Game Over with retry. Victory after boss.
- Audio: synthesized WebAudio SFX (punch, blast, hit, pickup, powerup, roar) and ambient music loop with simple arpeggio? Optional but adds life. Make simple procedural background music with oscillators, toggle sound. Must resume audio on user gesture.

UI style: neon anime: gradient sky, bold italic font (system fonts; use Google Font? offline risk; use system stack with heavy weights), orange/blue palette like Goku gi; energy yellow glow. Health bar orange gradient; ki bar cyan. Dragon ball icons gold with red stars.

Title screen: 3D scene background gameplay camera orbiting arena; title with big stroke text; "TAP TO BEGIN"; character select? Keep one hero. Small text "Drag to look • Joystick to move • Buttons to fight".

Implement with pointer events, support multitouch (joystick left, camera drag right, buttons). Prevent default touch gestures; fullscreen web app meta; safe-area CSS env; viewport-fit=cover.

Orientation: phone/tablet support both landscape and portrait; recommend landscape. Responsive CSS: in portrait show "rotate device" hint? Better support both: HUD adapts; in portrait buttons still at bottom, joystick bottom-left. Camera FOV adjusts. Add a subtle "↻ Rotate for best view" hint that appears in portrait but doesn't block.

Performance: shadows? Use PCFSoft shadow map 1024 with directional light but limited objects; mobile fine. Could avoid shadows for perf but shadows add depth. Use fake blob shadows (circle mesh) for characters and real shadow for arena? Use single dir light with shadow map 1024, arena receives. Should be OK in SwiftShader though screenshot capture might be slow. Keep renderer pixelRatio min(devicePixelRatio, 2) but in SwiftShader resolution 390x844 fine. Desktop 1440x900 also fine.

Post-processing bloom: UnrealBloomPass on mobile may be heavy with SwiftShader. Use additive glowing sprites/meshes instead. Maybe use a simple custom "glow" sprite texture from canvas radial gradient. Good.

## Game Design: "DRAGON ORB: CELESTIAL CLASH"

Genre: 3D arena action / beat-'em-up with flight dash, mobile-first.

Setting: Sky Temple arena floating above clouds at sunset; ancient stone platform with pillars, dragon statue, floating rocks, orange-to-purple sky, big sun.

Objective: Survive 4 waves, defeat Onyx Warlord boss. Collect 7 Dragon Orbs from defeated foes: when all 7, Shenron wish restores health and unleashes shockwave (nice). Use orbs? Maybe orbs just auto collect (fly toward player when near). HUD shows 7 slots fill. Wish triggers heal + supercharge.

Player: Kai — orange gi, blue belt/wristbands, spiky black hair, super saiyan transformation (gold hair + aura) when power meter full and POWER pressed.

Controls:
- Left virtual joystick: move.
- Drag anywhere right half: rotate camera (yaw/pitch).
- Right buttons: STRIKE (combo melee), BLAST (ki projectile), DASH (burst move with i-frames), POWER (transform when meter full; otherwise "charge" ki quickly). Also a lock-on indicator auto.
- Keyboard desktop: WASD/arrows move, J/Z attack, K/X blast, Shift dash, Space power, mouse drag camera.
- Aim assist: attacks auto-target nearest enemy in front / lock-on nearest.

Stats: HP 100, Ki 100 regen 10/s, Power meter fills by dealing/taking damage, transform at 100: 10s gold aura, +50% damage, +25% speed, ki regen boost.

Enemies:
- "Shade" (melee purple imp): approach, telegraph (red flash) then swipe; hp 45.
- "Seer" (ranged floating hooded): keeps distance, charges orb then fires slow projectile; hp 35.
- Boss "Onyx Warlord": large armored brute with horns, hp 420, uses charge, ground slam with shockwave rings, and beam sweep. Phases at 50% enraged.
- Enemy health bars floating (billboard sprites) maybe HTML overlay projected? Simpler: 3D billboard sprites (canvas health bar textures). Use canvas textures updated per enemy? That's costly but small. Alternative: small 3D bars (two planes) facing camera. Better: DOM labels? Keep in-world simple sprite bars using canvas generated once? Health changes; we can use two planes scaled: dark background + red fill with debug; billboard via lookAt camera each frame. Good.

Combat feel:
- Hits: freeze-frame (hitstop 60ms), screenshake, impact flash (ring + particles), damage numbers as sprites floating up (DOM overlay? simple sprite canvases). Use DOM floating numbers projected to screen — nice and cheap: create div each hit with CSS animation, project position. Limit count.
- Melee: 3-hit combo with alternating poses: right punch, left punch, spin kick. Range 2.6, arc 120°. 3rd hit stronger knockback.
- Dash: 0.18s burst at 26 speed, i-frames; leaves afterimages (ghost meshes). Cooldown 1.2s.
- Ki blast: glowing blue orb projectile with trail, homing slight, damage 14, cost 12.
- Charge: hold POWER to charge ki? Transform is more exciting. Let's make POWER button: tap toggles/activates Super when meter full; if not full, hold to charge ki + power (glow). Implement hold detection: pointerdown starts charging (adds ki/power, aura particles), pointerup: if meter full and short? Hmm overlapping. Simpler: POWER button always "CHARGE": hold to charge ki and power meter, release; when power meter full, automatically transform (with roar, flash) or show "SUPER READY" and tap POWER transforms. Could do: if power>=100 and not transformed → tap activates transformation instantly. Else hold = charge. Implement pointer down: if ready → transform on down; else charging while held. This is intuitive: when SUPER READY glows gold, tap.
- Movement while charging slower.

Enemy attacks and dodge with dash.

Waves:
Wave 1: 3 Shades. Wave 2: 4 (2 shade 2 seer). Wave 3: 5 (3 shade 2 seer). Boss wave: Onyx + 2 seers maybe.
Between waves: banner "WAVE 1" then "FIGHT!". Orbs: enemies drop orbs; first 7 kills total across waves? With total enemies 3+4+5+2+boss = 15, if every kill drops an orb, 7 reached mid wave 3. Orbs get attracted within 4m; player must move to collect. Show 7 ball HUD slots with stars. Wish: heal 40 + screen flash + dragon flying overhead + all enemies damaged?
